correctness.rationale: The cyclic 3+3 metric triangle inequalities are equivalent to |r_i−r_j|≤min(L,s) and r_i+r_j≥max(L,s). For sum-zero coefficients on an equilateral source A, the Lipschitz dual norm is (L/2)∑|c_i|. Cyclic-averaging any scalar extension does not increase norm; its coefficients α_i sum to 1 and each (b0,a_i) yields K r_i≥L|1−α_i|. Summing gives K≥2L/S, and identity on A gives K≥1; scalarizing a Banach-valued extension by a unit vector/support functional preserves this lower bound. If 2rmax≤S the positive α_i=1−2r_i/S attain upper bound for all A−B pairs; cyclic B−B difference has L(maxα−minα)=2L(rmax−rmin)/S≤2Ls/S. If rmax>sum other u+v, α_p=v/(u+v), α_q=u/(u+v), α_h=0, the metric enforces u+v≥L, s≥rmax−u>v, making all A−B and B−B ratios≤1. Equality boundary is continuous. For a planar 120° orbit the Pompeiu triangle-of-distances inequality guarantees three-support and S(x) threshold 2L. Independently evaluated all source Lipschitz-ball extrema and all 15 pairs on 3573 feasible rational six-point metrics, 3348 three-support and 225 two-support, reproducing exact K in both phases; infinite case follows analytic construction, not tests.
